approachQuestion.prompt: A rooted ordered tree is supplied as an immutable list of node depths in preorder, with root depth 0. Nodes are numbered by list position. The n depths, 1 <= n <= 200,000, are guaranteed to describe one valid tree: every later depth is positive and increases by at most one from the previous depth. Return the parent index of every node, using -1 for the root. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total time. Input: [0,1,2,1,2,2]. Output: [-1,0,1,0,3,3]. Node labels are only indices; no child lists are supplied.

options.text: Keep the active path as a stack of indices. Before node i at depth d, pop until path length is d. Its parent is the remaining top, or -1 for the root; then push i.
options.feedback: The first d active indices are exactly the ancestors of the next preorder node. Trimming removes finished branches while retaining its parent.

options.text: Set every nonroot parent to i-1.
options.feedback: In the example, node 3 has depth 1 and parent 0, not the previous node 2 at depth 2.

options.text: For each nonroot node, scan backward until finding the nearest preceding node at depth exactly one less.
options.feedback: That nearest ancestor is the correct parent, but repeated backward scans across completed branches can revisit many entries; the active path retains the needed ancestor.

options.text: Save the first node ever seen at every depth; use the saved node at depth d-1 as each new parent.
options.feedback: In the example, node 4 must have parent 3, but the first depth-1 node is 1, from an earlier branch.

feedback.reason: Preorder finishes a branch before visiting its next sibling, so a depth change identifies which active ancestors remain.
details: Process preorder positions in order. Trim the index stack to the incoming depth, report its top as parent (or -1 at the root), and push the new index. Each finished branch is removed before the next sibling branch begins.

Before a node at depth d, trim the active path to d ancestors. Its remaining top is its parent; a sibling replaces the old branch rather than becoming its child. Preorder indices retain the requested original identities.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For ancestor-index-frontier, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The input is immutable and excluded from auxiliary space. Returned output is excluded, but all working buffers count even if later copied into output.
Fixed-size integers, characters, indices and comparisons take constant time. Arithmetic is unit cost under the stated range guarantee.
Use an iterative implementation with a preallocated n-entry array and a top index: push and pop take constant time. No recursion, hashing, or hidden whole-buffer copies occur.
Materializing output takes time proportional to its length; no persistent snapshots or string concatenation are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each node index is pushed once and removed at most once from the active path.
details: Each node is pushed once and popped at most once, so total time is O(n), including writing n parent indices. A chain has depth n-1 and retains n path indices. That working path counts as O(n) auxiliary space even though the returned parent array is excluded.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A chain-shaped tree has n live ancestor indices in the working path, separate from the returned parent array.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each preorder node is pushed once and removed at most once when a later depth ends its branch.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: All n parent entries must be written, so merely reading logarithmically many depths cannot produce the complete result.
